title: Fastlane SDK embedded integration scaffold + smoke tests (draft)
content:
Goal: produce a tiny, repeatable onramp for engineers to embed a Redwood SDK call into a real app in ~15 minutes and have CI smoke tests that validate the happy path + a few common failure modes.

Background/context:
- We have many SDK onboarding docs and long-form playbooks (lots of words). This doc is intentionally focused: a runnable scaffold + minimal smoke-test CI that can be wired into starter repos (node + python + mobile demo).
- Naming: working name = "fastlane" (rwd-fastlane cli). Idea: single command generates an app skeleton + test harness + local dev stack (mock server) and a GitHub Actions smoke pipeline.

What this artifact should deliver (MVP):
1) rwd-fastlane CLI: scaffold command with templates for "node-server", "python-flask", and "nextjs-ssr".
2) Local dev stack: lightweight mock Redwood API container (fastlane-mock) that supports: streaming chunked responses, auth-token validation, kv-cache stubs, and configurable delays.
3) Code samples: 3 sample flows per template: simple text generation, streaming chat, embeddings call (small).
4) Smoke test suite: minimal e2e tests that run against fastlane-mock and assert token usage, request shape, and response fallback behavior.
5) CI job: GitHub Actions workflow snippet that runs smoke tests in PRs and gates merging (failures are non-blocking for early adopters, optional set to block for integrated teams).
6) Telemetry contract: minimal events the scaffold emits (sdk.init, sdk.call.start, sdk.call.end, sdk.error) and sample log lines for local troubleshooting.

Quickstart script (developer flow):
- prereqs: node 18+, python 3.11+, docker
- steps:
  1) npx rwd-fastlane new hello-node --template node-server
  2) cd hello-node && docker compose up -d (starts fastlane-mock + infra)
  3) export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=test_key
  4) npm install && npm run dev (app starts, hits mock)
  5) npm run smoke (runs smoke tests against mock)

Scaffold details:
- File layout for node-server template (minimal):
  - src/index.js (server + example call)
  - src/rwd-client.js (thin wrapper around fetch + telemetry hooks)
  - tests/smoke/basic.spec.js (jest + supertest pointing at mock)
  - .github/workflows/smoke.yml (installs deps, runs docker compose, runs npm run smoke)
  - docker/docker-compose.fastlane.yml (fastlane-mock + prometheus-lite optional)

fastlane-mock capabilities (stretch list):
- /v1/generate: supports regular and streaming (chunked transfer-encoding) paths
- /v1/embeddings: returns deterministic vectors for test inputs (hash -> vector)
- simulate latency: FASTLANE_DELAY_MS env var
- error injection toggles: return 429, 500, or partial body
- auth checking: requires header x-rwd-api-key=test_key
- record call metadata to /debug/calls (for smoke assertions)

Smoke tests (examples):
- basic-happy-path: make a generation call and assert 200 + expected token-ish string present
- streaming-happy-path: open stream, assert chunks arrive and stream closes cleanly
- retry-on-429: mock returns 429 first, succeed second attempt; assert client retried once
- fallback-variant: client configured with fallback model id; mock returns 504 and fallback is used instead
- telemetry-events: assert that sdk.init and sdk.call.end events were emitted and contain correlation id

CI job (github actions snippet idea):
- name: "Fastlane smoke"
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Start fastlane mock
      run: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.fastlane.yml up -d --build
    - name: Wait for mock
      run: ./scripts/wait-for-port.sh localhost 8080 30
    - name: Install and test
      run: |
        npm ci
        npm run smoke

Telemetry / logs / troubleshooting:
- Telemetry events (MVP) (strictly minimal):
  - sdk.init {sdk_version, env, template}
  - sdk.call.start {operation, request_id, model}
  - sdk.call.end {request_id, status_code, elapsed_ms}
  - sdk.error {request_id, error_code, message}
- For local dev the client prints to stdout and also hits /debug/calls on the mock so tests can assert events.

Developer experience goals/constraints:
- must be low-friction: single npm/npx command preferred to global install
- emulate production shapes but simplified: real SDK call shapes with minimal config
- must not require real Redwood credentials for onboarding flow (use test keys + mock)
- example apps should feel real (small UI for stream viewer; endpoint showing embeddings similarity) but stay tiny

Observability checklist for the scaffold:
- [ ] smoke tests exercise streaming + non-streaming code paths
- [ ] clear guidance in README for switching from mock -> real API (env vars, required model names)
- [ ] local debug endpoint shows last 10 calls with JSON payloads
- [ ] telemetry contract documented and easy-to-extend

Failure injection plan (for teaching/DI labs):
- network-latency: set FASTLANE_DELAY_MS=500 to show latency-sensitive behaviors (timeouts, spinners)
- chunk-splitting: split streaming payload into many small chunks to test UI buffer logic
- kv-cache-miss: have mock return cache_miss flag to force cold-start path in runtime
- partial-responses: return truncated body (simulate OOM / model cut-off)

Open questions / decisions to make: (brief)
- Should rwd-fastlane be JavaScript-only or distributed as a tiny Rust binary for speed + single executable distribution?
- What scope do we want for telemetry in-built in starter apps? (MVP = local print + debug endpoint; next = optional telemetry opt-in)
- How opinionated should client wrappers be? Provide a single tiny wrapper with explicit hooks rather than full-featured SDK surface.

Implementation TODOs (next steps):
- [ ] Proto: implement rwd-fastlane new with node template (owner: Sofia) — target: 2025-02-21
- [ ] fastlane-mock basic server (owner: Ethan) — target: 2025-02-24
- [ ] smoke tests (owner: Priya) — target: 2025-02-28
- [ ] GitHub Actions snippet + test on sample repo (owner: Liam) — target: 2025-03-05
- [ ] Internal demo + feedback session (invite: devx team + solutions eng) — target: 2025-03-10

Notes to self / quick ideas (scratchpad):
- Could reuse parts of existing local-mode tools (sdkenv-provisioning-labplay) but keep interface tiny
- Consider optional telemetry forwarder to a local file so users can grep during workshops
- Bundle a tiny web UI for streaming that shows each chunk with timestamps — great for demos

References / related tickets (scratch):
- DX-412: proposal to standardize starter templates
- GH PR: fastlane-scaffold initial (WIP) -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/fastlane-scaffold/pull/234

Raw checklist for a 15-min demo (script for presenters):
1) start: "we'll get a hello-world inference running in 15 minutes with no creds"
2) run: npx rwd-fastlane new demo-node --template node-server
3) cd demo-node && docker compose up -d
4) npm install && npm run dev (open the app in browser)
5) show streaming demo, open debug calls, run npm run smoke to prove tests pass
6) switch to real API: set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_URL and run again (optional)

End -- this doc is a working sketch. Intend to convert to a tiny repo with a README, CLI, and 3 templates. Will iterate on tests and mocking capabilities after first user workshop.

Unresolved: step-through for mobile/native init (ios/android). Might be a follow-up mini-template.
